To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spectral response of a photocathode is determined by the work functions, the electron affinity, the band gap, the Fermi level, the density of states, the surface states, and the surface recombination velocity of the materials used to fabricate the photocathode.

the spectra of the photoelectric response of composite cathodes with an oxide intermediate layer, consisting of a noble or transition metal and an alkali metal, are characterized by band-like spectra, with the exception of a few cases where the long wavelength maximum is missing.
The spectral photoelectric sensitivity of the compound cathode is characterized by the band-like character.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spectral photoelectric response of composite cathodes with oxide interlayers.
the spectral light sensitivity of composite photocathodes having an oxide intermediate layer.
the investigation of the spectral light-electric sensitivity of composite photocathodes with intermediate oxide layer, over a wide range of the spectrum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the photoelectric sensitivity of a composite photo-cathode, in the spectral region from 2000 to 600 Å, depends mainly on the nature of the alkali-metal layer, and that the nature of the carrier-metal layer has a relatively small influence.
the spectral response curves of the mixed photoemitters are of a band-like type.
the spectral sensitivity of composite photo-cathodes with oxide intermediate layer has a band-like character, in general, over a wide spectral range.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are not able to explain our experimental results in terms of photoelectric emission, but that they can be understood by means of the photoelectric emission of the metal and the secondary emission of the alkali metal.
we have studied a large variety of cathodes with a great variety of spectral response curves.
the photoelectric sensitivity curves for the composite cathodes with an intermediate oxide layer, investigated over a wide spectral range, show band-like characteristics in all cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spectral response of composite photo cathodes is not only determined by the band structure of the metal oxide but also by the band structure and work function of the metal.
the spectral sensitivity of a photocathode can be tailored by varying the metal and alkali metal components.
the spectral sensitivity curves of composite photocathodes with an oxide intermediate layer are of a band-like nature.
